solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird, dog also heard?

indicators.note: something heard reaches us by ear, so we go by how the words sound, not how they are written

blocks.note: a cocker is a cocker spaniel, a breed of dog, and 'too' means also

explanation.surface: Someone hears a bird and then a dog making the same noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'cocker too' runs together into COCKATOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot from Australia, so it is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Junior reporter on a Caribbean island

blocks.note: a cub reporter is a newcomer to journalism
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee journalist is sent out on a story to a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed on top of, so the young reporter sits above the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island nation in the West Indies, lying south of Florida.

clue.text: Bird runs into bovine

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a cow is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A bird dashes straight into a cow in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like the bird's movement, but R for runs is a cricket scorecard abbreviation and sits inside the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a large black bird of the genus Corvus, common across farmland.

clue.text: Manage to move inside tram

indicators.note: letters that move shift position, so their order is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A passenger struggles to shuffle along inside a crowded tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage to move' reads as one phrase about getting along the tram, but 'Manage' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to run or oversee it, a straightforward synonym for running affairs.

clue.text: Fancy bringing leader of negotiations into lecture

indicators.note: the leader of a group is at its front, so only the opening letter is wanted
bringing something into a place carries it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to orate is to deliver a speech or lecture
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fancies steering a lecture round to the topic of negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning to want to; it is the adjective. N goes inside ORATE to give ORNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fancy is elaborately decorated, which is exactly what ornate describes.

clue.text: Extra part of room, or extension

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece of it, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes an extra bit of a room, or an extension built on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'room' and 'or' and takes the first letter of 'extension'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, more means additional, so it can replace extra in a sentence.

clue.text: Shaped end of wood then too sharp

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so that is the only one kept
something shaped has been moulded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter whittles the tip of a piece of wood and makes it far too pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' sits naturally as a woodworking word, but here it means punctual, as in 'six o'clock sharp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at three sharp means exactly on time, the same idea as the idiom for precise punctuality.

clue.text: Mutated, the gene I figure

indicators.note: a mutated thing has changed its form, so the letters change their arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters

explanation.surface: A scientist announces that the gene they reckon on has mutated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' reads as a verb meaning to reckon; it is the noun, a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a numeral or number, and eighteen is one particular number.

clue.text: First of buds imminent in flower

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
something looming is about to happen

explanation.surface: The first buds on a plant are about to open into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening picture makes 'in flower' feel like part of the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is blooming has its blossoms open, the state described by being in flower.

clue.text: Deer with leg cut

indicators.note: something cut has been trimmed short, so its final letter is lost

blocks.note: a leg of a journey or race is a stage

explanation.surface: A deer has an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' looks anatomical, which suits a deer, but it means a stretch of a journey; dropping its last letter gives STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, so the word names a particular kind of the animal.

clue.text: Every bit of newspaper coverage ultimately in Vogue

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: 'every bit of the money' means 'all the money'
a rag is a slangy word for a poor-quality newspaper
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Every scrap of press coverage ends up in Vogue magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital V makes Vogue the fashion magazine, but the definition uses the ordinary phrase 'in vogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in vogue means currently fashionable, and the idiom for a popular craze says the same thing.

clue.text: Tenant is upset about losing money initially — monthly payment, say?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tenant is upset at losing money when the monthly rent falls due.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled tenant letters go around L and M. 'Say' marks a monthly payment as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one of a series of regular part-payments, of which a monthly one is an example.

clue.text: Talk with jazz fan about film director

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
Hitch was the nickname of the director Alfred Hitchcock

explanation.surface: A jazz lover chats about a favourite movie director.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitch was Alfred Hitchcock's well-known nickname, and cat is old jazz-age slang for a fan of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit-chat is light, casual conversation, so it is a kind of informal talk.

clue.text: Easy line composed in academic success

indicators.note: something composed has been put together anew, so the letters are arranged afresh
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a pass is success in an exam

explanation.surface: A student writes one easy line and still gets top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like calm or written, but it signals rearranging the line, and a pass is the basic exam success.
explanation.definitionFit: A painless task causes no trouble or effort, which is what an easy one is.

clue.text: Filly, say, kennelling a husky

indicators.note: kennelling an animal shuts it inside an enclosure, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a filly is a young female horse, so an example of one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young horse is somehow sharing a kennel with a husky dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog, which suits the kennel, but it is the adjective for a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, which is the same as a voice that is hoarse.

clue.text: Best or otherwise, pulsating light

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters

explanation.surface: Someone debates whether a flickering light is the best choice or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best or' reads as the start of a comparison, but those six letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp that flashes rapidly on and off, as used in discos and photography.

clue.text: Freezing ale

blocks.note: first meaning: piercingly cold, as of wind or weather
second meaning: a type of British draught beer

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a very cold pint; the two words are separate meanings. In Britain a bitter is a hoppy pale ale served in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind is icy cold, and in British pubs the word also names a hoppy draught beer.

clue.text: Fruity little things peeled tennis gear off

indicators.note: peeled off goes with the later word; stripped away carelessly, the letters land in disorder
off completes the phrase peeled off, and something knocked off its course is no longer in order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: After the match, a player peels off their sweaty tennis kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' seems to describe the fruit, which fits since these are peeled before eating, but with 'off' it signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerines are small sweet citrus fruits, so they are fruity little things.

clue.text: Some design a tooth that bites

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun: something that bites

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a portion of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word, through the second, into the third

explanation.surface: Some people design a set of false teeth that can bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tooth that bites' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'that bites', for a biting insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small fly, and many gnats bite people to feed on blood.

clue.text: Equine sound in chestnut about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: chestnut and bay are both reddish-brown horse colours, and a bay is a horse of that colour
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse makes a noise somewhere near the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut' could be the nut or tree, but here it is a horse colour, matching the equine theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A bray is the loud harsh cry of a donkey, which is a member of the horse family.

clue.text: Follow four letters from the editor

indicators.note: taking four letters from a phrase lifts a short consecutive run out of it

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A writer is told to follow a few letters of advice sent by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence from the editor, but it simply counts the characters to lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow advice is to pay attention to it and obey, which is the meaning of heed.

clue.text: Failing isn’t rare for device with holes

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A faulty gadget full of holes is, sadly, a common sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' looks like part of a judgement on the gadget, but the whole of 'isn't rare' is the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or colander, a kitchen tool full of small perforations for draining.

clue.text: Assignment while filling empty truck

indicators.note: an empty container has nothing in its middle, so only the outside letters remain
filling something puts material inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A worker's job is to load up a truck that has been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: AS sits between T and K, the outer letters left when truck is emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignment is a piece of work given to someone, which is what a task is.

clue.text: Clerical author, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so we go by the spoken form

blocks.note: J. B. Priestley was the English playwright who wrote An Inspector Calls

explanation.surface: An author is said to be churchy in manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's surname has an extra E but is pronounced exactly like the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical means relating to the clergy, and priestly describes what belongs to or suits a priest.
